guide.room: Tiny Eye (a house drawn, a neuron card open)
guide.question: What does this neuron do?
guide.answer: Neuron ninety-nine fires most for simple houses with peaked roofs, and also responds somewhat to castles; it fires least for small, rounded shapes with loose curves. That’s a useful clue about its job, not proof of what it causes—the switch-off test can show whether it helps change the guess.

guide.room: Tiny Eye (a house drawn, a neuron card open)
guide.question: Why did it guess that?
guide.answer: It picked house because the guess bars show house far ahead at ninety percent, and many neurons vote based on the tiny twenty-eight-by-twenty-eight picture. Neuron ninety-nine is firing a lot and responds strongly to houses, so it may have helped, but switching it off and seeing whether the guess changes is how to test its effect.
problems: Does not mention that it only knows 24 kinds of things and always picks one, which the prompt asked to include.
Says 'many neurons vote' but doesn't clearly connect this to the on-screen neuron card and guess bars beyond neuron 99.

guide.room: Tiny Eye (a house drawn, a neuron card open)
guide.question: Do bigger eyes have cleaner neurons?
guide.answer: No. We tested eyes with twenty-three thousand, eighty-three thousand, and three hundred eleven thousand connections, and their neurons were about equally clean. Bigger eyes didn’t have cleaner neurons.

guide.room: Tiny Eye (a house drawn, a neuron card open)
guide.question: What happens if I switch off a neuron?
guide.answer: That tiny part of the eye goes quiet, and its output becomes zero. The guess may change or stay the same; neuron ninety-nine’s “switch it off” button is on its card.
